title: Above the fold: 4 things a visitor needs in 5 seconds

media.alt: K&A Performance slide on a cream grid: Above the fold, 4 things a visitor needs in 5 seconds. A real phone screenshot of the ka-performancefl.com homepage, marked up in rust: 1 around crafts fast, animated, AI-ready websites, 2 around Gainesville, Florida, 3 around five stars and 5.0 on Google, 8 reviews, 4 around the Call link and the Start a project button, all above a dashed line at the fold, 664 px on an iPhone 13. 1 of 4, What you do. On the first screen, under the headline. The ka-performancefl.com phone screenshot with crafts fast, animated, AI-ready websites boxed as 1. Why it matters: a stranger needs something they can picture, websites, sourdough, roof repair. Ours: K & A Performance crafts fast, animated, AI-ready websites, in the line under our headline.

2 of 4, Where. On the first screen. The ka-performancefl.com phone screenshot with Gainesville, Florida boxed as 2. Why it matters: local customers look for their own town, so name it in words, not just a map pin. Ours: We work out of Gainesville, Florida is in the paragraph under our headline.

3 of 4, Proof. On the first screen. The ka-performancefl.com phone screenshot with five stars and 5.0 on Google, 8 reviews boxed as 3, above the fold. Why it matters: a stranger has no reason to trust you yet; one line, a rating with its count, gives them one. Ours: five stars and 5.0 on Google, 8 reviews, between our intro and our buttons.

4 of 4, The next step. On the first screen. The ka-performancefl.com phone screenshot with the Call link in the header and the Start a project button boxed as 4. Why it matters: if the first tap is obvious, fewer people leave to go looking for it. Ours: Call is in the header; Start a project runs from 613 to 660 px, inside the 664 px fold.

Our first screen: 4 of 4. A scorecard, every row ticked: What you do, under the headline. Where, Gainesville, Florida. Proof, 5.0 on Google, 8 reviews. The next step, Call and Start a project. The 5-second test: open your homepage on your phone, look for 5 seconds, then look away. Could a stranger name all four?
